claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys contain deposition-induced strain.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys contain interfacial defects.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys contain localized short-range order.
Deposition-induced stresses and defects generate mechanically derived short-range order.
MSRO governs the magnetocaloric response of as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys during low-field cooling cycles.
MSRO governs hysteresis in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys during low-field cooling cycles.
MSRO mediates the magnetostructural transition by modifying magnetostructural coupling.
MSRO lowers local energy barriers for spin reorientation.
Lower local energy barriers reduce the abruptness of the first-order magnetic transition.
The MSRO-mediated broadening of the transition decreases hysteresis.
The MSRO-mediated changes can lower hysteresis while retaining a sizable magnetocaloric entropy change.
Controlled post-deposition annealing can partially relax deposition-induced stress without completely erasing local chemical ordering.
Changing deposition rate can modulate the degree of MSRO.
Annealing that reduces deposition-induced stress will reduce MSRO.
Samples with moderated MSRO will show a broader and more gradual magnetostructural transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Samples with moderated MSRO will show lower thermal hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
Samples with moderated MSRO will show a shift in peak entropy change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type baseline has a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with a large, hysteretic entropy change.
The magnitude of hysteresis reduction and entropy-change tuning depends on MSRO, grain size, and residual-stress distribution.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that more MSRO lowers energy barriers, broadens the transition, and decreases hysteresis, while the intervention is described as reducing stress and thus MSRO yet is predicted to broaden the transition and decrease hysteresis further. No non-monotonic or optimum-MSRO relationship is stated to reconcile these opposite causal directions.

The as-deposited baseline is said to contain deposition-induced stress and localized MSRO, which the mechanism says should broaden the transition and lower hysteresis, but the same baseline is described as having a sharp, strongly hysteretic first-order transition.
